newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissho to invest in Sri Lanka power project.
newsitem.headline: Nissho to invest in Sri Lanka power project.

text.p: Nissho Iwai Corp said on Monday that it will provide a total of about $14 million in investments and loans to an electric power project in Sri Lanka.

The Japanese trading house will provide $4.0 million in investments and $10 million in loans to Asia Power (Pvt) Ltd, a joint venture between John Keells Holdings Ltd and KHD Great Britain, the company said in a statement.
Nissho Iwai's investment accounts for about 18 percent of the joint venture's capital.
KHD Great Britain, a unit of Germany's Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG said last week it had started construction of a 51-megawatt thermal power plant in a suburb of the Sri Lankan capital.
The $62 million diesel-powered plant, to function on a build, own and operate (BOO) basis, will add approximately 16.5 percent more power to the island's grid.
The plant's entire output will be purchased by the state power utility Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB).

Nissho Iwai said it will be the first time for the company to take part in a project by a private electric power firm in Sri Lanka. The trading company said it has previously taken part in such projects in the Philippines, Pakistan and the United States.
